A Quarter Century of Impact
🌳
Monumental Afforestation Drive
Launched and drove the historic Green Kalam Initiative, achieving the landmark goal of planting over one million tree saplings across Tamil Nadu — restoring ecological balance and expanding green cover statewide.
🌱
Visionary Leadership & Legacy
Catalyzed by the inspiration of former President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, uniting civic leaders, administrative officers, Padmashree Vivekh, and the youth of Tamil Nadu toward sustainable environmental stewardship.
🍃
Grassroots Educational Outreach
Engaged educational institutions — hosting the landmark event at Krishnasamy College of Engineering & Technology, Cuddalore — embedding environmental responsibility into student culture and community life.
🌿
Sustained Environmental Impact
Over 25 years of relentless action, converting local tree-planting drives into an enduring statewide movement that continues to combat climate change and enhance biodiversity.
KCET's Legacy & Commitment to Green Initiatives

The Green Kalam Project — a movement against global warming — was born when Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam planted an idea in Padmashree Vivekh: "To propagate the importance of trees. Why don't you start planting them as an inspiration to others?" This sparked a noble initiative with the vision to plant 10 lakh tree saplings across Tamil Nadu. By June 2012, the count had surpassed 14 lakh saplings — exceeding the target by 40%.

KCET did not merely host this event — it embodied its purpose. The college's green campus on the Nellikuppam High Road became the chosen venue for Tamil Nadu's most significant environmental celebration, drawing India's most beloved scientist to Cuddalore. That Dr. Kalam chose KCET's grounds to plant a sapling, sign the movement's banner, and deliver his keynote is a distinction this institution carries with enduring pride.

Today, as KCET celebrates its Silver Jubilee, the Green Kalam legacy lives in every tree on campus, in every student who learned that engineering serves not just industry but the planet — and in Dr. Kalam's own autograph, signed at KCET, which remains one of the institution's most treasured memories.

When India's Missile Man stood at Cuddalore's campus for a Greener Planet
In KCET's 11th year, the college became the chosen venue for one of Tamil Nadu's most significant environmental movements. Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam — scientist, President, Bharat Ratna — stood at KCET's podium to celebrate one billion trees for one billion people. That evening of 7th June 2012 belongs permanently and proudly to KCET's 25-year story. The green cover it inspired continues to grow — just as KCET has grown — across every passing year.
